Use Android Designs as the current default icon.
Affects the launcher icon and app identity shown in notifications and other system surfaces. Some launchers may refresh after a short delay.
Open the native app language settings for i18n testing without changing the system language.
Android native per-app language settings; falls back to the app info page when the direct page is unavailable.
Unable to open app language settings. Open this app in system settings and choose Language.
Keep the current rhythm for page switches, search bars, sheets, and expand transitions.
Use direct show/hide transitions to reduce extra animation cost on weaker devices.
Affects the launch screen fade, main page switching, search bars, bottom bar visibility, expandable areas, and common capsule press transitions.
System back gestures preview the previous page while dragging, making hierarchy clearer.
Back gestures return directly, reducing visual distraction from page previews.
Affects system back gesture previews on Settings, About, Guide, and other navigation-stack pages.

Theme mode, launcher icon style, and system language entry.
Main-page retention, warm data, and guide-media preload strategy.
Home highlights, dynamic backgrounds, and motion-time visual strategy.
Manage page transitions and interaction motion.
Page switching, search bars, expandable areas, and predictive-back motion.
Manage ActionBar, bottom bar, and card feedback visuals.
Liquid Glass style for switches and Toast. ActionBar, Sheet, and Dialog are always Liquid Glass.
Toast interruption, search focus, and grip-aware floating buttons.
Manage non-Home background image switches, assets, and opacity presets.
Background switch, image selection, clearing, preview, and suggested settings.
Image fitting, anchor, page style, and depth motion.
Opacity, color intensity, and reading overlay presets.

Use v2 Liquid Glass switches, buttons, and capsule controls for consistent liquid interaction.
Use solid capsule fallback and the Miuix switch style for consistent low-load visuals.
Affects Settings, sheets, business-page button groups, and page configuration controls.
Use side tilt with a small touch fallback to place floating buttons on the easier side.
Keep floating buttons on the right side to avoid position jumps from false positives.
Affects OS / GitHub add and search buttons, plus the MCP start-stop button. Off by default.
Keeps adjacent main pages, warms target-page data, and prefetches guide cover/gallery media for faster switching and return visits.
Keeps only the current main page and loads guide media on demand, fitting memory-tight or heat-sensitive devices.
Affects main-pager beyond-viewport pages, BA warm data, guide-page preloading, and static media prefetch.
Home icon and title HDR highlight
Enable linked highlight effects for the Kei icon and KeiOS title. The effect is brighter with the screen on.
Disabled by default. Enabling this can trigger HDR highlight output.
Affects the linked highlight on the Home Kei icon and KeiOS title. Enabling this can trigger HDR.
Keep full dynamic background and glass strength while scrolling Home, paging, and tapping.
Use the regular Home dynamic strategy during motion to control burst rendering cost.
Affects the Home dynamic background, Home overview-card glass, and Home top ActionBar effects during motion.
Non-Home pages show a custom background image while keeping the current layout and layering.
Non-Home pages use the default solid background.
Affects OS / MCP / GitHub / BA and other non-Home main pages.
Background image set. It applies when entering non-Home pages.
Keep the image ratio and fill the screen. Best for images already cropped to the device shape.
Keep the full image centered. Best when preserving the whole picture matters.
Force the image to fill the screen. Best for abstract images where slight distortion is acceptable.
Preserves the top of the image first. Best for upper-body subjects or top-heavy details.
Preserves the center of the image first. Works well for most wallpapers and cropped images.
Preserves the bottom of the image first. Best when the subject sits lower in the image.
Preserves the left side first. Best for wide images with a left-leaning subject.
Preserves the right side first. Best for wide images with a right-leaning subject.
Uses the current opacity and overlay settings with a clearer background presence.
Lowers image presence and adds a page overlay for text-heavy pages.
Gently softens the background while preserving the mood.
Prioritizes content readability for input, feedback, and Shell pages.
Moves the background slightly while switching main pages for extra depth.
Keeps the background static to control burst rendering cost while paging.
Affects horizontal switching on OS / MCP / GitHub / BA main pages. Standalone pages such as Settings and About keep a static background.
Previews the current non-Home background parameters. Real pages still add their own content density and glass layers.
Use this to check whether the image, opacity, anchor, and reading overlay keep text legible.
Current opacity: %1$d%%. Use preset stops for quick switching.
Recommended default: %1$d%%, balancing readability and atmosphere.
Current color intensity: %1$d%%. Lower it to keep busy images from competing with text.
Recommended default: %1$d%%, preserving the original image colors.
Current overlay: %1$d%%. Improves text readability for visually busy images.
Recommended default: %1$d%%, preserving the original background mood.
Compatibility bypass enabled (high risk): temporarily changes system network rules to trigger Super Island.
Disabled by default (recommended): reduces HyperOS status bar and System UI risk.
Applies only to the Super Island style. Live Update does not use this bypass.
Wait %1$dms after sending, then restore `com.xiaomi.xmsf` network access.
Only affects restore timing after enabling Super Island compatibility bypass. MCP / GitHub / BA Super Island notifications share this delay.
Recommended default: %1$dms. 8 Elite Gen5 can try 75ms; other devices should start from the default.
Use the Super Island template (Hyper Focus). Turn off to use AOSP Live Update notifications.
Currently using AOSP Live Update notifications. Turn on to restore the Super Island template.
Affects the visual style of MCP, GitHub, and BA AP notifications.
Automatically pop the summary when a Super Island notification is first sent; later progress updates stay quiet.
Only update the Super Island state on first send, reducing refresh interruptions.
Applies only to the Super Island style. Progress refreshes will not force repeated expansion.
Pop once when refresh starts, stay quiet after the user collapses it, then pop once when refresh finishes.
Pop once when refresh starts. Progress and final states stay in the summary.
Only update the Super Island summary for every state. Best for low interruption.
Affects MCP, GitHub, BA, and future notifications that reuse the Super Island template.
The Super Island and its focus notification stay until they are updated or cleared.
The system closes the Super Island and its focus notification after %1$s.
Affects MCP, BA, GitHub Actions and other Super Island notifications; GitHub refresh notifications keep their own short timeout.
This app is allowed to ignore battery optimization, improving MCP keepalive and background notifications.
System battery optimization is active, so background keepalive and real-time notifications may be reclaimed more often.
Unable to open battery optimization settings. Adjust it manually in system settings.
System background state is normal. Background refresh, reminders, and notification recovery follow Android scheduling policy.
Android background restriction is enabled for this app. Background refresh, reminders, and foreground-service starts will be heavily limited.
System battery saver is enabled, so background refresh and notification delivery may be delayed.
The device is in Doze idle mode, so background network and jobs wait for system maintenance windows.
Current standby bucket is %1$s. Background network, jobs, and alarms may be delayed more often.
Unable to open Android background settings. Adjust it manually from the app info page.
After reboot, app update, time, or time-zone changes, GitHub, BA, and WebDAV background schedules are restored automatically.
%1$s allows app auto-start. Keepalive services and notifications can recover more reliably after boot.
%1$s restricts app auto-start. Service recovery and background reminders may be delayed after boot.
%1$s provides an auto-start management page. Current status cannot be read; open it to check manually.
This device has no stable OEM shortcut. The button opens this app in system app info for permission and background management.
This device has no separate OEM auto-start permission page. The app follows the system default startup policy.
No separate entry on this device
Unable to open OEM auto-start settings. Check the system security app manually.
Notifications are allowed, so live reminders, background notices, and keepalive status can display reliably.
Notification permission is restricted, so MCP status, background reminders, and keepalive notifications may fail to display.
Unable to open notification settings. Adjust it manually in system settings.
Currently reading the app list through the %1$s privileged channel, covering a wider installed-package scope.
Currently using direct system app-list reading, suitable for normal local app matching.
App-list access is limited, so imported or matched local apps may have a narrower visible scope.
Unable to open app-list related settings. Check permissions on the app info page manually.
Privilege mode is off. KeiOS will not connect to Shizuku, request root, or run privileged commands.
Privileged commands run through the Shizuku service. Start Shizuku and grant access first.
Privileged commands run through su. Requires a superuser manager such as Magisk, KernelSU, or APatch.
Applies to OS page commands, app-list detection, and MCP privileged tools
This mode offers the shell channel only. Managed install and the UID firewall fall back to command-line paths.
Root is granted. Privileged commands run through su.
Root is unavailable. Related advanced capabilities fall back to direct system mode.
Grant permission again in your superuser manager
Shizuku is connected. App-list detection and some system capabilities prefer the Shizuku channel.
Shizuku authorization is unavailable. Related advanced capabilities fall back to direct system mode.
Grant permission again in Shizuku Manager
The privileged channel is ready. KeiOS can read secure settings and record its own self-check state.
Enable an available Shizuku or Root mode to check the secure-settings channel and improve self-guard diagnostics.
Checks the KeiOS privileged channel, foreground service, boot/update check, and screen-on check state.
Runs a low-priority persistent service to help KeiOS keep background check capability.
Records one KeiOS self-guard check after system boot or this app updates.
Runs a throttled self-guard check when the screen turns on, useful on stricter background-control devices.
This policy serves KeiOS persistence and diagnostics, reads only necessary state, and records local history.
Applies to this app self guard only. Local history is excluded from WebDAV sync.
Manual checks are written to local self-guard history. Exported JSON helps diagnose keepalive failures.
Records manual check, foreground service, screen-on, boot, and app-update self-guard results.
Run a manual check or enable a self-guard policy to show the latest result here.
Full copy mode: text uses system selection with long press, drag handles, select all, and the system text menu.
Lightweight copy mode: long-press an item to copy “title: value” with system haptics and lower interaction cost.
Only text joins system selection. Buttons, pills, links, and other interactive content leave the selection area to reduce gesture conflicts.
Uses lightweight copy everywhere for smoother scrolling. Enable this temporarily when drag selection or select all is needed.
Review per-page cache usage and clear selected or all items.
Count cached items, storage size, and recent activity across pages.
Skip cache directory and storage traversal to reduce extra Settings-page cost.
Settings reads cache summaries from GitHub / MCP / System / BA and other pages.
Use v2 Liquid Glass Toast, displayed at the upper-center of the screen to avoid obscuring content.
Use Android system Toast, displayed at the bottom of the screen.
Hide low-priority prompts such as run completed, copied, and cleared. Error and permission prompts still appear.
Allow low-priority prompts to appear as lightweight Liquid Glass Toast messages.
Only disables Settings-page cache diagnostics. Page caches and normal usage remain active.
Cache diagnostics are disabled. Settings will skip cache size, update time, and cleanup stats.

Record local KeiOS logs as needed, export a ZIP, and generate a GitHub Issue draft.
Controls the minimum local file-log level.
Review log size and latest writes, then export or clear logs.
Controls the minimum level written by KeiOS AppLogger to local log files.
Only affects KeiOS AppLogger local file logs, covering active app logging points for GitHub, MCP, notifications, Shizuku, performance probes, and BA remote fetches.
Pick a level before reproducing an issue, then export the ZIP or generate a feedback draft afterward. Clear logs after diagnosis.
Low-overhead mode is active. Existing logs can still be exported, cleared, and used for feedback.
Focus the input and open the keyboard after expanding the search bar.
Expanding the search bar shows the input first; tap the input to open the keyboard.
Affects main search bars such as About, Settings, OS, GitHub, and Catalog.
Reuses animation resources to reduce repeat downloads. Resources not used recently are cleared automatically.
Display the system WebView directly. The device selects its graphics backend. Applies the next time you open a viewer.
Keep the original WebGL materials and present frames on a native canvas for devices with texture composition issues. Up to 60 fps. Applies the next time you open a viewer.
